title: Kill Ring Surgeon
desc: Fix broken commands by cutting and pasting. Typing works too, but every letter costs a key.

levels.title: Chop the tail
levels.tip: The cursor is already in the right spot. One key does it. (Ctrl+C restarts a level if you slip.)

levels.title: Lose the junk
levels.tip: The mirror image of Ctrl+K. Both put what they cut in the kill ring, shown below the line.

levels.title: Hop forward
levels.tip: Alt+F jumps to the end of the next word. Hop to the right spot, then cut.

levels.title: Hop back
levels.tip: Alt+B jumps back to the start of a word. Punctuation like '-' counts as a gap between words.

levels.title: Word muncher
levels.tip: Ctrl+W cuts the word before the cursor. It only stops at spaces, so node_modules goes in one bite.

levels.title: Stutter
levels.tip: Alt+D cuts the word after the cursor, including the space in front of it.

levels.title: Move a word
levels.tip: Everything you cut lands in the kill ring. Ctrl+Y pastes it back wherever the cursor is.

levels.title: Sudo, please
levels.tip: Ctrl+A jumps to the start of the line. Cut the last word, jump, paste, tidy the space.

levels.title: Too much force
levels.tip: Ctrl+E jumps to the end of the line, however far away it is.

levels.title: Wrong way round
levels.tip: Sometimes it's cheaper to move the first argument than the last.

levels.title: One big bite
levels.tip: Cuts made back to back join into one kill ring entry, so one Ctrl+Y brings them all back.

levels.title: Dig in the ring
levels.tip: The kill ring keeps your last ten cuts. Ctrl+Y pastes the newest; press Alt+Y right after to swap it for the one before.

levels.title: Spin the ring
levels.tip: After Alt+Y, Ctrl+Y keeps pasting from where you stopped in the ring. Keep pressing Alt+Y to go further back.

levels.title: Full surgery
levels.tip: Everything at once. Hint: a paste can carry a space along with a word.
